title: Novel Compound Heterozygous RECQL4 Pathogenic Variants and Associated Phenotypes in a Chinese Patient With Rothmund‐Thomson Syndrome: Case Report and Literature Review
abstract: ABSTRACT                                        Background                                            Rothmund‐Thomson syndrome (RTS) is a rare autosomal recessive disorder characterized by poikiloderma, sparse hair, short stature, skeletal abnormalities, and an increased predisposition to malignancies. Pathogenic variants in the                       RECQL4                       gene represent the most common genetic cause of RTS type 2. However, the full phenotypic spectrum, particularly regarding endocrine manifestations, remains incompletely understood.                                                                                Objective                                            To report novel compound heterozygous                       RECQL4                       pathogenic variant in a Chinese patient, describe a previously unreported endocrine phenotype (gynecomastia), and provide a comprehensive review of the literature regarding the                       RECQL4                       mutational spectrum and differential diagnosis.                                                                                Methods                     A comprehensive clinical evaluation, including detailed physical examination, dermatoscopic assessment, and histopathological analysis, was performed. Whole‐exome and Sanger sequencing were conducted to identify the causative variants. A literature review was additionally performed to contextualize the clinical and genetic findings.                                                           Results                                            A 14‐year‐old boy presented with classical poikiloderma, short stature, and an unreported feature of gynecomastia associated with low testosterone levels. Genetic testing identified compound heterozygous variants in                       RECQL4                       : a known nonsense variant c.2290C>T (p.Glu764*) and a novel frameshift variant c.2053del (p.Asp685Thrfs*5). Our literature review further delineated the differential diagnosis of poikiloderma among related genodermatoses and highlighted the systemic impact of                       RECQL4                       dysfunction.                                                                                Conclusion                                            The identification of the novel c.2053del variant broadens the known mutational landscape of                       RECQL4                       . Furthermore, the integration of our newly observed endocrine phenotype with a literature review underscores the necessity of multidisciplinary evaluation—including endocrinological, orthopedic, and audiological assessments—in the comprehensive management of RTS.
